payload.webank_role: Working capital for your Shenzhen shops, optional custody of your savings pot in a sub-account in your company's name, and a buffer planned never to be drawn.

bank_cards.label: WeBank 微业贷 for your home shops
bank_cards.covers: Documented needs of your shops at home: stock, seasonal wages, a Shenzhen refit. Nothing in Singapore
bank_cards.cost: Interest at the rate WeBank offers you
bank_cards.conditions: Sized to the real need net of your own funds, and only up to your usual borrowing level

source.label: 流动资金贷款管理办法 (2024) Art. 6 and the annex formula

bank_cards.note: While your WeBank borrowing is above your usual level, your Singapore set-aside and transfers pause. They restart once it's back to normal.

bank_cards.label: FX and transfer at the bank that registers your ODI
bank_cards.covers: Converting to Singapore dollars and sending to your Singapore company
bank_cards.available_from: After lender consent, the ODI filing and the bank registration (R4)
bank_cards.cost: That bank's FX spread and fees
bank_cards.conditions: Your WeBank statements go to that bank as proof the money is the company's profit and your savings

later_cards.label: Singapore loans after opening: EFS working capital, bank SME loans
later_cards.covers: Working capital for the Singapore shop once it trades
later_cards.available_from: After opening. EFS: once a local partner holds at least 30%. Banks: usually after 6 to 12 months of trading (market practice)
later_cards.cost: Interest; EFS loans are partly risk-shared by Enterprise Singapore
later_cards.conditions: Never counted in this plan (R8). EFS needs at least 30% local shareholding and sets no trading-history test

product.label: Enterprise Singapore: EFS SME Working Capital Loan
